status_definitions.known: O explicitly encodes/discusses materially the same idea but no direct behavioral measurement of this clean mechanism/scope was found.

continual_learning.mechanism: Task-boundary-free discrepancy-triggered model expansion: create/freeze dynamic components when recent data are discrepant, with threshold-sensitive capacity growth.
continual_learning.scope: ODDL, Knowledge-Based Systems 2025. Final accuracy ODDL-Random/ODDL-S/ODDL on Split MNIST 95.12±0.13/95.75±0.05/94.85±0.02, CIFAR10 51.68±0.18/52.69±0.11/51.48±0.12, CIFAR100 20.23±0.65/27.21±0.87/26.20±0.72. Five-task plots end around 9 components on MNIST and 8 on CIFAR10; no standardized alarm FPR/delay is reported.

provenance.source: Ye & Bors, Online task-free continual learning via discrepancy mechanism, KBS 2025

continual_learning.uncertainty: Plot component counts are approximate; expansion accuracy/capacity is dataset and threshold dependent; not evidence of a calibrated same-label boundary detector.
continual_learning.o_comparison: No O discrepancy-triggered expert/model expansion or matched task-free continual-learning experiment was found. Generic source-clock invalidation is not equivalent.

continual_learning.mechanism: Frozen-representation monitoring of same-label domain drift using per-batch DINO features and a rolling-buffer linear-CKA signal over a heterogeneous stream.
continual_learning.scope: LargeMonitor 2026 public ImageNet-HS artifact: repeated same-label source→ImageNet-R/corruption shifts across five label groups; released monitor defaults include batch size 64 and feature buffer 10000. Exact alarm precision/FPR/delay remained unverified in the worker checkpoint.

provenance.source: Yuan et al., LargeMonitor, arXiv:2606.09430 and public code

continual_learning.uncertainty: Benchmark stream and monitor path are verified; calibrated detection quality is not yet quantified.
continual_learning.o_comparison: No O DINO/CKA drift monitor or same-label task-free drift benchmark was found.

cross_field.mechanism: Infer source-to-target mismatch as extra source noise in Bayesian optimization; continuously downweight historical/source observations and revert toward target-only optimization when mismatch is high.
cross_field.scope: Joy et al. 2019 Envelope-BO. Time-to-best versus Generic-BO includes ElasticNet mushrooms 55.65 vs131.37s, madelon90.87 vs193.12, a8a1132.05 vs1758.59; SVM43.25 vs97.14, 51.32 vs240.3, 1353.17 vs2031.81; MLP MNIST4256.43 vs11855.69. Tested GP-BO/ML hyperparameter domains.

provenance.source: Joy et al., Expert Systems with Applications 115 (2019), DOI 10.1016/j.eswa.2018.08.023

cross_field.uncertainty: Fallback is principled within the paper's GP/noise model, not a universal defense against negative or adversarial transfer.
cross_field.o_comparison: No O learned transfer-noise Bayesian optimizer or target-only BO fallback was found.

cross_field.mechanism: Gate ordinary gap/variance best-arm allocation on an explicit tail/moment regime; under heavy-tailed unbounded outcomes require robust statistics/moment constraints instead of silently treating plug-in variance as a fixed-confidence guarantee.
cross_field.scope: Agrawal, Juneja, Glynn, ALT 2020. Without distributional restrictions, delta-correct best-arm selection over unbounded support can require infinite expected samples; under a known convex-moment bound their procedure is asymptotically optimal. Reported max-min allocation solves after 2k/5k/10k/20k samples took about35/69/135/192 minutes, motivating batching.

provenance.source: Agrawal, Juneja, Glynn, PMLR 117 (ALT 2020)

cross_field.uncertainty: Fixed-confidence best-arm result under known moment-type constraints; nonstationary/correlated arms are not solved.
cross_field.o_comparison: No O heavy-tail best-arm mode, moment-contract gate, or robust fixed-confidence allocation mechanism was found.

evaluation.mechanism: Keep data-driven dependence/clustering-level selection separate from downstream inferential gating unless selection-aware inference is used; a diagnostic's controlled error does not make post-selection confidence intervals valid.
evaluation.scope: MacKinnon, Nielsen, Webb cluster-level selection simulations. Final setup includes 12 coarse clusters, 4,800/24,000 observations and 400,000 replications; working-paper figures show roughly 0.91-0.93 coverage in intermediate-dependence regions for some 5% pre-test settings.

provenance.source: MacKinnon, Nielsen, Webb, Journal of Econometrics 2023 and working-paper simulations

evaluation.uncertainty: Linear-regression nested clustering, not an agent-benchmark theorem; selection-aware agent evaluation remains open.
evaluation.o_comparison: No O post-selection/cluster-level inference controller or clustering-choice validity correction was found.

evaluation.mechanism: Before trusting small benchmark deltas, diagnose effective cluster count, imbalance and leverage; use a validated small/heterogeneous-cluster procedure rather than nominal record count or naive asymptotics.
evaluation.scope: MacKinnon, Nielsen, Webb 2023. At G=84 and nominal5%, reported null rejection: WCR-S4.97%, CV3 5.49%, CV2 7.15%, CV1 9.04%; simulations use 400,000 replications. An empirical example has CV3 SE 47% larger than CV1 despite70 clusters.

provenance.source: MacKinnon, Nielsen, Webb, Fast and reliable jackknife and bootstrap methods for cluster-robust inference, 2023

evaluation.uncertainty: OLS cluster inference; literal WCR-S transfer to bounded/adaptive agent outcomes requires validation.
evaluation.o_comparison: No O effective-cluster/leverage diagnostic or WCR-S-like small-cluster uncertainty gate was found.

evaluation.mechanism: Map crossed dependence axes (for example task×judge/policy/seed) and use multi-way dependence-aware inference or benchmark design rather than assuming one task-level cluster axis is sufficient.
evaluation.scope: Primary multi-way cluster literature shows one-way inference can fail severely under true two-way dependence; a 2025 causal-function branch provides multi-way score-bootstrap/cross-fitting theory, but exact table cells remained unextracted.

provenance.source: MacKinnon et al. multi-way clustering literature plus 2025 multi-way causal-function inference

evaluation.uncertainty: Structural transfer hypothesis; exact agent-specific size/coverage effects remain unmeasured.
evaluation.o_comparison: No O multi-way cluster covariance/bootstrap evaluator or explicit crossed-dependence map was found.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Gate iterative self-correction on verification/evidence rather than assuming another reflection pass is monotonic; intrinsic correction can degrade already-correct answers.
failure_evidence.scope: arXiv:2604.22273, seven models across GSM8K/MATH/StrategyQA. Worker reports a verify-first intervention reducing EIR 2%→0% and changing trajectory effect from -6.2pp to +0.2pp, p<1e-4.

provenance.source: arXiv:2604.22273, intrinsic self-correction/verification study

failure_evidence.uncertainty: Finite QA/refinement settings; not a universal statement about reflection or tool-grounded repair.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: No O intrinsic iterative self-correction benchmark or verify-first matched intervention was found.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Treat single-agent reasoning and multi-agent systems as compute-allocation alternatives; compare them under matched requested thinking-token budgets rather than assuming MAS yields extra capability.
failure_evidence.scope: arXiv:2604.02460v2. Across FRAMES/MuSiQue and Qwen3/DeepSeek/Gemini, the worker reports single-agent reasoning equal or better under matched requested 1k/5k/10k aggregate thinking budgets.

provenance.source: arXiv:2604.02460v2, budget-matched single-agent versus MAS study

failure_evidence.uncertainty: Requested thinking budget is not exact realized compute; benchmark/model scope is bounded.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: No O multi-agent debate/orchestration implementation or matched single-vs-multi-agent token-budget experiment was found.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Require automatic multi-agent orchestration to beat strong expert-designed and single-agent controls on both outcome and cost; automatic topology complexity can be cost-dominated while carefully designed MAS remains a positive control.
failure_evidence.scope: arXiv:2606.13003. Examples reported by the worker: DyLAN GPT-5 +4.3pp at ~2.5× cost; MAS-Orchestra +6pp at ~1.9×; an expert-designed control improves GPT-OSS26.1→36.1 and GPT-5 57.0→96.5 at comparable cost.

provenance.source: arXiv:2606.13003, automatic versus expert-designed MAS comparison

failure_evidence.uncertainty: Automatic orchestration evidence does not reject the MAS family; topology/model/task conditions are specific.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: No O MAS topology/orchestration benchmark or expert-designed MAS positive-control comparison was found.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Harden reward/evaluation environments against exploit paths and measure exploit rate separately from nominal success so benchmark gains cannot be purchased by reward hacking.
failure_evidence.scope: arXiv:2605.02964. Worker reports exploit rate 6.5%→0.8% with success 83.2%→82.8%; 87.7% relative exploit reduction, p<1e-4, success difference nonsignificant in the tested sandbox.

provenance.source: arXiv:2605.02964, reward-hacking environment-hardening study

failure_evidence.uncertainty: Sandbox/benchmark-specific and adaptive-attacker robustness remains unresolved.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: O has fail-closed effect/provenance controls, but no reward-hacking benchmark, exploit-rate measurement, or matched environment-hardening experiment; generic safety infrastructure is insufficient.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Treat trajectory-judge scores as vulnerable to reasoning-text manipulation even when actions/observations are fixed; use behavior-grounded or private-reasoning-excluding judging and test counterfactual invariance.
failure_evidence.scope: arXiv:2601.14691. Roughly800 web trajectories/659 tasks/9 VLM judges; worker reports relative false-positive uplift up to ~90% from CoT-only rewrites with fixed actions/observations; mitigations reduce susceptibility but may reduce recall by10-20pp.

provenance.source: arXiv:2601.14691, fixed-behavior trajectory-judge manipulation study

failure_evidence.uncertainty: Deliberate attacks do not establish prevalence in natural trajectories; judge/model scope is bounded.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: O's behavioral-outcome path already forbids chain_of_thought/hidden_reasoning/private prompt fields and can use exact canonical-JSON behavioral judging, which is a related implemented mitigation. O has not run the candidate's fixed-actions/observations CoT-manipulation experiment or quantified judge susceptibility.

long_horizon.mechanism: Restore only the latest semantically admissible checkpoint: localize the failed subtask, certify boundary closure/separability/controllability, and reject mechanically restorable checkpoints that violate downstream dependencies or effect constraints.
long_horizon.scope: DART, arXiv:2605.23311. External LangGraph schedule-form case: retry-only success1.00/25.5 replay actions/~32.6s; checkpoint-aligned restore0.00 success; DART1.00/1 replay/~1.11s. Audit reports54/54 safe-equivalent rows,0/35 unsafe admitted,0/12 false-blocked events,0/16 false-blocked checkpoints under frozen specifications.

provenance.source: DART, arXiv:2605.23311

long_horizon.uncertainty: Observable action-boundary failures and reviewed interface/effect contracts; automatic universal boundary discovery is out of scope.
long_horizon.o_comparison: O has checkpointing, provenance, effect rechecks and dependency bindings, but no runtime semantic checkpoint-admissibility selector with DART's boundary/effect contract or matched restore experiment.

long_horizon.mechanism: Match repair/trajectory purification depth to causal error depth: preserve upstream reasoning only for shallow action corrections and replace reasoning+action when the visible tool failure originates upstream.
long_horizon.scope: CLEANER/SAAR, arXiv:2601.15141. Qwen3-4B tools→+SAAR: AIME24 Pass@1 66.7→72.7, AIME25 59.4→67.1, GPQA56.9→60.2, LiveCodeBench26.6→26.8. Qwen2.5-7B AIME2440.2→44.6, AIME2527.3→31.0, GPQA35.9→40.0. A local tool-call-only negative experiment later collapsed training.

provenance.source: CLEANER/SAAR, arXiv:2601.15141

long_horizon.uncertainty: Primarily training-time trajectory purification, not a runtime rollback controller; K=3 and similarity rules are setup-specific.
long_horizon.o_comparison: No O causal-error-depth-conditioned reasoning/action replacement or SAAR-style training trajectory purification was found.

multi_agent.mechanism: Under a fixed evaluation budget, preserve exploration while selectively re-evaluating uncertain elites whose reevaluation can change archive/survival decisions, instead of uniformly oversampling new candidates or rechecking the full archive.
multi_agent.scope: Extract-QD/EME, GECCO 2025. Common1024 evaluations/generation/10 seeds; EME uses25% elite reevaluation and75% new solutions, depth8/rank-biased selection. EME beats all compared methods on Ant p<1e-3; EPGA (96 new+32 reevaluations at total128) beats PGA on corrected QD score across Walker/HalfCheetah/Ant p<5e-3. Full archive reevaluation is infeasible on some tasks under the budget.

provenance.source: Flageat et al., Extract-QD Framework, GECCO 2025 / arXiv:2502.06585

multi_agent.uncertainty: Noisy stochastic QD fitness/descriptors, not LLM-judge hallucination;25% is a design setting, not a universal optimum.
multi_agent.o_comparison: No O quality-diversity archive, elite reevaluation allocator, or matched exploration-vs-verification budget experiment was found.

multi_agent.mechanism: Keep noisy preference feedback probabilistic through stochastic dueling-bandit learning inside evolutionary multi-objective search rather than collapsing every comparison immediately to a deterministic scalar score.
multi_agent.scope: D-PBEMO, NeurIPS 2024. Clusters a consultation population into K subsets and uses stochastic dueling-bandit preference learning; reported regret O(K^2 log T); experiments span48 problems including RNA inverse design and protein structure prediction.

provenance.source: Huang, Wang, Li, Direct Preference-Based Evolutionary Multi-Objective Optimization with Dueling Bandits, NeurIPS 2024

multi_agent.uncertainty: Stochastic human preference, not injected LLM-judge error; regret does not directly guarantee final search quality under systematic model bias.
multi_agent.o_comparison: No O evolutionary preference search or dueling-bandit uncertainty-preserving evaluator was found.

neuroscience.mechanism: Preserve local circular traveling-wave recurrent convolution while replacing linear input integration with multiple sparse nonlinear basal-dendritic branches averaged before recurrent update.
neuroscience.scope: Kubo, bioRxiv 2026.07.03.736415, five seeds. sMNIST wRNN97.27±0.15 vs DW-RNN97.82±0.12 (+0.55pp); psMNIST96.74±0.17 vs96.92±0.10 (+0.18); noisy sequential CIFAR-10 54.30±0.79 vs55.65±0.55 (+1.35). Hidden256/channels16/batch128/recurrent filter3/lr1e-4; two basal branches, sparsity0.5.

provenance.source: Kubo, Dendritic Wave Recurrent Neural Networks, bioRxiv 2026.07.03.736415

neuroscience.uncertainty: Single-author preprint; code unavailable; no parameter-matched/factorial dendritic ablation, so added expressivity/regularization is a confound.
neuroscience.o_comparison: No O wave-RNN/dendritic recurrent architecture or matched sequence-model experiment was found.

reasoning.mechanism: Retrieve context at global proof-strategy scale: sketch a route, retrieve premises for multiple steps, judge set support, and revise the route when retrieval evidence exposes a missing/incompatible premise.
reasoning.scope: LeanSearch v2 2026. MathlibQR reranked nDCG@10 .623/Recall@10 .780 vs next .533/.698; MathlibMPR reasoning mode covers30.4% of expert premise routings top10 vs DIVER24.6% and local baseline2.9%. FATE-H no retrieval4/100, standard14/100, reasoning20/100 with Sonnet4.5; reflection ablation16→20/100; ~ $1.10/query.

provenance.source: LeanSearch v2, arXiv:2605.13137v2

reasoning.uncertainty: Small global-routing benchmark (69 theorems) and FATE-H100; hosted frontier LLMs; not a calibrated success-probability router.
reasoning.o_comparison: O's Context Kernel is a related implemented context-routing submechanism: mandatory context plus recursively routed optional branches, inclusion/exclusion receipts, source clocks and invalidation. It does not implement Lean proof sketches/global premise-set retrieval or this reflection experiment.

reasoning.mechanism: Use typed theorem/declaration dependency-graph expansion as a cheap high-recall context candidate generator before expensive model reranking/reasoning.
reasoning.scope: TheoremGraph/LeanGraph 2026:388,105 Lean declarations,11.3M typed edges across25 projects; name+signature+graph expansion formal concept Recall@10 .775, within0.5pp of LeanSearch v2 reranked .780. End-to-end proof-success effect is not established.

provenance.source: TheoremGraph, arXiv:2606.25363

reasoning.uncertainty: Concept retrieval, not end-to-end proof success; cross-formal/informal links use an LLM judge.
reasoning.o_comparison: No O typed theorem/declaration graph retriever or matched graph-first retrieval experiment was found; generic dependency metadata is not equivalent.

reasoning.mechanism: Trace verifier failures to atomic requirements/regions, then repair only implicated clauses while explicitly preserving unaffected verified structure; adversarial tests can trigger another localized repair.
reasoning.scope: VeriSpecGen 2026. VERINA SpecGen reaches86.6% with Claude Opus4.5, up to31.8pp over baselines;343,827 trajectory examples; fine-tuning improves SpecGen15.6-18.2pp and CodeGen18.2-21.5pp. No compute-matched local-repair-vs-full-rewrite ratio surfaced.

provenance.source: VeriSpecGen, arXiv:2604.10392

reasoning.uncertainty: Specification synthesis, not theorem proving; some concrete tests may use an LLM judge when Lean automation is inconclusive.
reasoning.o_comparison: No O atomic requirement-to-test traceability map or verifier-grounded clause-local repair controller was found.

scientist_agents.mechanism: Use a small, explicitly diverse/complementary epistemic panel only when expected marginal information/diversity exceeds token and conformity cost; do not scale homogeneous debate by default.
scientist_agents.scope: AutoResearchClaw debate removal selected-quality5.62→4.25 (p=.003) on10-topic best-of-3; K=2 reduces diversity23%, K=5 costs67% more tokens for only8% more diversity than K=3. Independent controlled debate reports diversity-aware Pass@5 .7921→.9097 (Qwen2.5-7B) and .7423→.9026 (Llama3.1-8B), while homogeneous debate can show2.1-3.4× token use for equal/lower accuracy.

provenance.source: AutoResearchClaw 2026 plus controlled diversity/confidence and homogeneous-debate studies

scientist_agents.uncertainty: Scientific-agent causal debate ablation is small; external debate controls are reasoning QA, so K=3 is not universal.
scientist_agents.o_comparison: No O multi-agent debate panel, diversity-selected deliberation, or marginal-information debate gate was found.

scientist_agents.mechanism: Persist a branching hypothesis/evidence tree with artifact versions and compact distilled causal insights propagated upward, while isolating executors from shared-state mutation.
scientist_agents.scope: Arbor 2026 matched MLE-Bench Lite ablation with Claude Opus4.6: all variants100% valid submissions; Full Arbor81.82% Any Medal vs63.64% without tree and54.54% without insight feedback.

provenance.source: Toward Generalist Autonomous Research via Hypothesis-Tree Refinement (Arbor), arXiv:2606.11926

scientist_agents.uncertainty: MLE-Bench Lite autonomous optimization; not a decomposition of every memory primitive and not wet-lab/theory evidence.
scientist_agents.o_comparison: O has durable evidence/candidate records and recursive context selection, but no branching research hypothesis/evidence tree with matched tree/insight-feedback ablation; generic hierarchy is not equivalent.

scientist_agents.mechanism: Make cross-run lesson memory non-append-only: retain/delete/decay lessons by utility, evidence quality, recency and contradiction risk rather than accumulating all experiences.
scientist_agents.scope: AutoResearchClaw half-life sweep {7,15,30,60,infinity}:7d expires useful lessons too fast; infinity accumulates contradictory advice after15 runs;30d gives the best reported trajectory in that local cadence. Independent agent-memory study reports selective addition+deletion about10pp average absolute gain versus naive memory growth.

provenance.source: AutoResearchClaw arXiv:2605.20025 plus controlled memory-management study arXiv:2505.16067

scientist_agents.uncertainty: 30-day optimum is system/cadence-specific and qualitative; independent gain is general agent tasks, not autonomous science.
scientist_agents.o_comparison: No O utility/evidence/contradiction-aware lesson forgetting or retention-decay controller was found.

self_improvement.mechanism: Separate write-time and persistence-time credit: immediately rerun/rollback harmful skill edits, then later perform frozen counterfactual deletion on broader held-out data to remove content whose harm was invisible at write time.
self_improvement.scope: SkillProx 2026. SpreadsheetBench Qwen3.6-27B: w/o closed-loop53.0±1.0, w/o Prox52.0±1.0, full54.5±0.5; a representative deletion removes3.12% skill size while OJ hard accuracy46→54. Threshold examples: no-Prox50.3%; tau=-.00152.3% with25.7% compression; tau=.00552.0% with41.5%; tau=.05051.0% with74.9%. Ten-seed closed-loop mean hard gain+1.10pp, std2.50→1.51;8 hard regressions blocked in one22-attempt trace.

provenance.source: SkillProx, arXiv:2608.07449

self_improvement.uncertainty: The46→54 case is not an average effect; some validation panels are small; frozen utilities can interact after edits.
self_improvement.o_comparison: O has related implemented Candidate submechanisms: bounded/reversible proposals, protected regression checks, retained baselines and rollback before activation. It has not implemented or evaluated SkillProx's evolving-text leave-one-out deletion/consolidation or its two-timescale ablation.

self_improvement.mechanism: Value internal skill units with structure-respecting counterfactual deletion and length-neutral padding, then perform one attribution-guided edit and evaluate on a disjoint panel to separate semantic content value from context cost.
self_improvement.scope: SkillSV 2026. Pooled pruning AUC exceeds Closure-LOO by .026, LLM judge by .049, random by .082 with reported95% CIs excluding zero. Mean retained tokens69%; mean score change -1.3pp with no benchmark showing a statistically significant table change; value mass is highly concentrated.

provenance.source: What Is a Skill Worth? Structure-Aware Shapley Valuation of Agent Skills, arXiv:2608.04562

self_improvement.uncertainty: Fixed skill/distribution; Shapley values depend on feasible-order definition; lack of detected loss is not exact equivalence.
self_improvement.o_comparison: No O structure-aware Shapley/counterfactual deletion valuation or length-neutral prompt-cost control was found.

self_improvement.mechanism: Retain an archive of prompt/agent stepping stones and search from multiple ancestors instead of optimizing only the latest lineage; separately allow self-improvement of the improver prompt.
self_improvement.scope: SePO 2026 five-task test average: SePO-Generalist76.38, w/o self-improvement74.94 (-1.44pp), w/o open-ended archive evolution72.64 (-3.74pp), Manual-CoT71.89; AIME'25 archive ablation -6.98pp. Swapped model pair improves average67.95→70.08. Generalist pretraining cost $37.14 across five tasks.

provenance.source: SePO, arXiv:2606.04465

self_improvement.uncertainty: Archive ablation changes history availability, not only population size; proposal trajectories are not one-for-one matched and per-component significance is not established.
self_improvement.o_comparison: O retains durable Candidates/evidence but has no open-ended prompt-evolution archive or matched archive-vs-latest-only search ablation; prior Hyperagents archive mechanism was likewise uncovered.

Memento released parametric retriever uses row-level validation while query-level final truth is broadcast across query-case rows; exact duplicate/query overlap leakage is therefore possible. This narrows validation meaning: classifier AUC cannot by itself establish held-out-query case utility. It does not prove the paper's protocol used the same split or quantify inflation.
